analysis:
Reviewed the ProviderLoop.swift changes (head lines 705-716 and 868) and the DaemonState+Coding.swift patch. No security regression identified.

ProviderLoop.swift adds only in-memory actor state: selectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride, savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch. savedEnabledModels is initialised at line 868 from config.config.backend.enabledModels. These changes touch no wire protocol, attestation, key custody (keyPair at line 908 is still NodeKeyPair.generate() per process), encryption, App Attest authorization or prefix-cache storage paths. The test-only override at line 709 is internal, nil in production, and typed as an optional Sendable closure, so it adds no externally reachable surface.

DaemonState+Coding.swift adds four optional fields (enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch, selectedModelRecovery, plus the new CodingKey cases) with decodeIfPresent/encodeIfPresent. Decoding is backward compatible. Content is model IDs and recovery entries, which are operator-local state-file data, not consumer prompts (A-001), keys (A-003) or tokens (A-008). Model IDs are already public via heartbeats, so the extra disclosure is low. The patch excerpt was truncated, so the SelectedModelRecoveryEntry type and other state-file encoding were not visible.

Unverified integration questions for later passes: (1) the companion ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift is not supplied. A recovery load that bypasses eviction, weight-hash verification or the retiring and failed-self-test tombstones (retiringModels, failedSelfTestHashes) would affect T-027 and T-012. (2) How savedEnabledModels from the config file feeds switching or advertisement is not visible; reading config from the operator-writable filesystem is within TB-003. (3) Whether SelectedModelRecoveryEntry carries any error strings with sensitive paths. No cited line shows a concrete issue, so findings are empty.
